content:
Key Takeaways

Importing a used car to Mozambique requires careful preparation, proper documentation, and understanding of customs procedures at Maputo Port. This guide provides the complete roadmap for successful vehicle importation in 2026.

Understanding Mozambique Vehicle Import Requirements

To import a used car to Mozambique successfully, you must comply with specific age restrictions, documentation requirements, and safety standards set by the Mozambican Customs Authority (Autoridade Tributária de Moçambique). Vehicles older than 8 years for passenger cars and 10 years for commercial vehicles are prohibited from importation as of 2026.

The Mozambican government implemented these age restrictions through Decree 23/2018 to improve road safety and reduce environmental impact. All imported vehicles must meet Euro 4 emission standards minimum, and right-hand drive vehicles are accepted since Mozambique follows left-hand traffic patterns inherited from Portuguese colonial administration.

Pre-shipment inspection is mandatory for all vehicles valued above $3,000 USD. This inspection must be conducted by an approved inspection company such as Intertek, SGS, or Bureau Veritas at the country of origin. The inspection certificate is valid for 45 days from issuance date.

Vehicle Age and Condition Standards

Passenger vehicles must not exceed 8 years from the year of manufacture, while commercial vehicles and trucks can be up to 10 years old. The calculation is based on the first registration date, not the model year. For example, a 2018 model registered in 2019 would be considered 7 years old in 2026.

All vehicles must be in roadworthy condition with functioning safety equipment including seatbelts, lights, brakes, and mirrors. Accident-damaged vehicles requiring structural repairs are generally rejected unless professionally restored with proper documentation.

Essential Documentation for Maputo Port Vehicle Import

The complete documentation package for importing a used car through Maputo Port includes the original vehicle title, bill of sale, shipping documents, pre-shipment inspection certificate, and customs declaration forms. Missing or incorrect documentation is the leading cause of clearance delays at Maputo Port.

According to Maputo Port Authority statistics from Q1 2026, approximately 23% of vehicle shipments experience delays exceeding 10 days due to documentation issues. Proper preparation significantly reduces clearance time and associated storage costs.

Required Documents Checklist

  • Original vehicle title or certificate of ownership
  • Commercial invoice or bill of sale showing purchase price
  • Pre-shipment inspection certificate (PVOC or equivalent)
  • Bill of lading from shipping company
  • Packing list detailing vehicle specifications
  • Insurance certificate covering transit period
  • Import permit from Ministry of Industry and Commerce
  • Customs declaration form (DU - Documento Único)
  • Payment receipts for all applicable duties and taxes

Import Permit Process

The import permit application must be submitted to the Ministry of Industry and Commerce at least 30 days before the anticipated arrival date. The permit costs 2,500 Meticais (approximately $40 USD) and requires submission of vehicle specifications, intended use declaration, and proof of financial capacity to pay applicable duties.

Processing typically takes 15-20 business days, though applications submitted during peak seasons (November-February) may take longer due to increased volume. Electronic submissions through the government's online portal expedite processing compared to paper applications.

Mozambique Customs Duty Vehicle Calculation

Vehicle import duties in Mozambique are calculated based on the CIF (Cost, Insurance, Freight) value using a combination of ad valorem rates and specific duties. The total tax burden typically ranges from 45% to 75% of the vehicle's declared value, depending on engine size, age, and type.

The customs duty structure implemented in 2026 includes a base import duty of 25%, VAT at 17%, and additional fees including customs processing (0.75%), port handling, and inspection charges. Luxury vehicles with engines exceeding 3.0 liters face additional luxury tax of 10%.

Duty Calculation Example

For a used Toyota Corolla 1.6L valued at $8,000 CIF:

  • Import Duty (25%): $2,000
  • VAT (17% on CIF + duty): $1,700
  • Customs processing fee (0.75%): $60
  • Port handling charges: $150
  • Total taxes and fees: $3,910
  • Total cost including vehicle: $11,910

Maputo Port Vehicle Import Process

The Maputo Port vehicle import process begins with vessel arrival notification and typically takes 7-14 days for complete clearance when all documentation is properly prepared. The port operates dedicated vehicle terminals with specialized equipment for car carrier vessels and container operations.

Maputo Port handled approximately 18,500 imported vehicles in 2025 according to port authority records, with German and Japanese vehicles comprising 65% of total imports. The port's strategic location provides efficient access to Mozambique's major population centers and neighboring landlocked countries.

Step-by-Step Clearance Process

  1. Arrival Notification: Shipping agent notifies customs of vessel arrival 48 hours prior
  2. Document Submission: Submit complete documentation package to customs broker
  3. Physical Inspection: Customs officials inspect vehicle against documentation
  4. Duty Assessment: Customs determines final duty calculation based on valuation
  5. Payment Processing: Pay all duties, taxes, and fees through authorized banks
  6. Release Authorization: Customs issues release order after payment confirmation
  7. Port Exit: Present release documents and collect vehicle from port

Common Clearance Challenges

The most frequent clearance issues at Maputo Port include valuation disputes where customs officials challenge declared vehicle values, documentation discrepancies between shipping papers and customs forms, and delays in payment processing through the electronic payment system.

Working with Customs Brokers and Agents

Licensed customs brokers are mandatory for vehicle imports through Maputo Port, as individual importers cannot directly handle customs procedures. Reputable brokers charge 3-5% of the CIF value plus fixed processing fees ranging from $200-400 USD depending on vehicle complexity.

The Mozambican Association of Customs Brokers maintains a registry of 156 licensed agents as of 2026, with approximately 30 specializing in vehicle imports at Maputo Port. Broker selection significantly impacts clearance speed and cost efficiency.

Selecting a Reliable Customs Broker

  • Verify current license status with customs authority
  • Request references from recent vehicle import clients
  • Compare fee structures and additional charges
  • Assess experience with your specific vehicle type
  • Confirm availability of storage facilities if needed

Port Facilities and Storage Options

Maputo Port offers secure vehicle storage areas with 24/7 security coverage and weather protection for extended storage periods. Standard storage fees are $12 USD per day for passenger vehicles, with discounted rates for storage periods exceeding 30 days.

The port's vehicle terminal includes inspection bays, washing facilities, and minor repair services for addressing cosmetic issues identified during customs inspection. Vehicle preparation services help ensure compliance with local road registration requirements.

Insurance and Risk Management

Marine cargo insurance is mandatory for vehicle imports and must cover the full CIF value plus 10% to account for additional costs. Leading insurance providers in Mozambique include Empresa Moçambicana de Seguros (EMOSE) and Hollard Moçambique, offering specialized vehicle transit coverage.

Insurance claims procedures require prompt notification within 72 hours of discovering damage, with professional surveyor assessment before vehicle release from port custody. Pre-shipment photography documentation supports successful claim resolution.

Insurance Coverage Options

  • Total loss coverage including theft and fire
  • Partial damage coverage for transport-related damage
  • Delayed arrival coverage for additional storage costs
  • Currency fluctuation protection for duty calculations

Vehicle Registration and Road Legalization

After customs clearance, imported vehicles must be registered with the National Institute of Transport (Instituto Nacional de Transportes - INT) within 30 days. The registration process requires customs clearance certificate, technical inspection at an authorized center, and payment of registration fees totaling approximately 15,000 Meticais.

Technical inspection includes emissions testing, safety equipment verification, and VIN number confirmation. Vehicles failing initial inspection can be re-tested after necessary repairs, with additional fees for each subsequent attempt.

Cost Planning and Budgeting

Total landed cost for importing a used car to Mozambique typically equals 160-180% of the original purchase price when including vehicle cost, shipping, duties, clearance fees, and registration expenses. Budget an additional 10-15% for unexpected costs or delays.

Recent Regulatory Changes and Updates

The Mozambican government implemented new electronic customs procedures in January 2026, requiring digital submission of all import documents through the SIDONIA World system. This modernization reduces processing time but requires broker familiarity with the new platform.

Environmental regulations introduced in 2026 mandate Euro 4 emission compliance for all imported vehicles, with stricter enforcement through enhanced inspection procedures. Vehicles failing emission standards face rejection or costly modification requirements.

Upcoming Changes for 2027

Proposed regulations under review include mandatory electric vehicle quotas for commercial importers, reduced age limits for certain vehicle categories, and implementation of blockchain technology for customs documentation. These changes aim to modernize Mozambique's vehicle fleet while improving customs efficiency.

Expert Tips for Successful Vehicle Import

Based on my experience as Vehicle Export Specialist at RosM Autos, successful Mozambique vehicle imports require meticulous preparation, realistic timeline expectations, and contingency planning for potential complications. The key is thorough documentation preparation and working with experienced local partners.

Start the import process at least 90 days before your desired delivery date to accommodate document preparation, shipping transit, and customs clearance. Rush shipments often result in higher costs and increased risk of complications.

Pre-Purchase Considerations

  • Verify vehicle compliance with Mozambican standards before purchase
  • Calculate total landed costs including all fees and taxes
  • Research local service and parts availability for your chosen vehicle
  • Consider seasonal demand fluctuations affecting shipping costs
  • Evaluate financing options for duty payments if needed

Common Mistakes to Avoid

The most costly mistake in Mozambique vehicle imports is underestimating total costs, leading to insufficient funds for duty payments and prolonged storage fees. Accurate cost projection prevents financial complications during the clearance process.

Inadequate documentation preparation causes the majority of clearance delays. Ensure all documents are properly notarized, translated if necessary, and accurately reflect vehicle specifications and transaction details.

Documentation Pitfalls

  • Inconsistent vehicle descriptions across documents
  • Missing or expired pre-shipment inspection certificates
  • Incorrect currency declarations on invoices
  • Inadequate proof of ownership documentation
  • Missing insurance coverage for full CIF value

Alternative Import Options

While Maputo Port handles the majority of Mozambique's vehicle imports, alternative entry points include Beira Port for central region destinations and Nacala Port serving northern provinces. Port selection affects shipping costs, transit times, and local clearance procedures.

Overland imports through South African border crossings offer cost advantages for certain vehicle types but require compliance with both countries' import regulations and additional transit documentation.

Professional Import Services

RosM Autos provides comprehensive vehicle export services to Mozambique, including pre-shipment inspection in Germany, customs-compliant documentation preparation, and coordination with reliable Maputo Port customs brokers. Our quality-assured vehicles meet all Mozambican import requirements, reducing clearance complications.

Our established relationships with shipping lines and local partners ensure efficient handling throughout the import process. We provide detailed cost projections and timeline estimates, helping clients plan successful vehicle acquisitions.

Conclusion

Importing a used car to Mozambique through Maputo Port requires careful planning, proper documentation, and realistic budget expectations. Success depends on understanding local regulations, working with experienced professionals, and allowing adequate time for all procedures.

The total process typically takes 45-60 days from purchase to local registration, with costs ranging from 160-180% of the original vehicle price. Proper preparation and professional guidance ensure smooth customs clearance and successful vehicle importation.
